learning_outcomes.text: Acquires basic knowledge about energy transmission systems. (Concepts of phasor, current, voltage, power, balanced three-phase systems)
Creates equivalent circuits for short, medium, and long transmission lines.
Derives current-voltage relationships for short, medium, and long transmission lines.
Defines concepts such as voltage regulation, line efficiency, steady-state stability limit, and natural loading.
Lists types of reactive power compensation in transmission lines.
Calculates current, voltage, and power for different loading conditions of the transmission system.
Performs per-unit modeling of transmission systems.
Learns modeling of positive, negative, and zero sequence circuits.
Performs mathematical analysis of the load flow problem.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to energy transmission systems, basic concepts related to transmission systems (phasor, current, voltage, power concepts, three-phase systems)
Transmission line parameters, calculation of line impedance and admittance elements (line resistance, inductance and capacitance)
Transmission line modeling, short line modeling, derivation of current and voltage relations, voltage regulation, line efficiency.
Modeling of medium-length lines, derivation of current-voltage relations for PI and T equivalent circuits, drawing of phasor diagrams
Modeling of long transmission lines, derivation of current-voltage relations, voltage regulation and efficiency.
A, B, C, D parameter determination and related example solutions
Maximum Power Transmission in Steady State
Per-unit concept, calculation of per-unit values of electrical quantities, per-unit conversion
Derivation of bus admittance matrix and related example solutions
